topics.title: Morbid Paradox
topics.text:
So, because there are $7.3$ billion people in the world right now and $2$ people die every second, the probability that I will die the next second is $\frac{2}{7.3 billion}$. I'd say that $4$ people are born every second, so there will be $2$ more people in the world every second. Therefore the probability that I will die the next second is $\frac{7.3 billion-2}{7.3 billion}*\frac{2}{7.3 billion+2}$, which is a smaller probability than the first second. The second after that is $\frac{7.3 billion-2}{7.3 billion}*\frac{7.3 billion}{7.3 billion+2}*\frac{2}{7.3 billion+4}$. As you can see, the probability that we die every second that passes gets smaller and smaller, and soon it will reach $0$. So the older we get, the more immortal we become...yet everybody dies someday. :(



Why is this the case?
